---
title: "Existing Repositories"
---

`repo-familiar` supports bootstrapping existing repositories as a deliberate second mode, separate from generating a brand-new downstream repository.

## Intended Flow

1. Advise on the existing repository to choose a stage, profiles, tools, and memory practice.
2. Audit the existing repository.
3. Detect existing agent files, docs, model profiles, skills, and generator metadata.
4. Produce a dry-run plan showing files to add, files that already exist, and conflicts.
5. Apply only selected additive changes.
6. Write or update `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` to record what was added.

## Safety Rules

- Do not overwrite user-owned files by default.
- Treat `--dry-run` as the default UX for existing repositories.
- Require explicit flags for replacing or adopting existing files.
- Keep secrets out of generated tool and model configuration.
- Separate generator metadata in `.repo-familiar/` from runtime agent assets in `.agents/`.

## Candidate Commands

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo --intent significant-refactor
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo --format json
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo --format json
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo --asset-group docs
uv run python -m repo_familiar resolve-conflicts --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --interactive
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-model --path /path/to/repo --model-profile default-coding --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-docs --path /path/to/repo --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill grill-with-docs --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-tool --path /path/to/repo --tool cq --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-tool --path /path/to/repo --tool browser-automation --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-tool --path /path/to/repo --tool opencode-homebrew-path --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-prompts --path /path/to/repo --prompt-profile prompt-migration-gpt55 --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-repomap --path /path/to/repo --repomap-profile hamilton-dag --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-safety --path /path/to/repo --safety-profile prompt-output-safety --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-privacy --path /path/to/repo --privacy-profile data-privacy-review --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-public-interest --path /path/to/repo --public-interest-profile child-rights-digital --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-sandbox --path /path/to/repo --sandbox-profile sandbox-light --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-secrets --path /path/to/repo --secrets-profile kvenv-azure-keyvault --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-secrets --path /path/to/repo --secrets-profile sops-age --sops-age-recipient age1... --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-design --path /path/to/repo --design-profile design-impeccable --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-worktree --path /path/to/repo --worktree-profile parallel-worktrees --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar check-skill-sources
```

`bootstrap-existing`, `add-model`, `add-docs`, `add-skill`, `add-tool`, and advisory profile add commands are dry-run by default. Pass repeated profile flags to choose specific assets. Pass `--apply` to write missing assets. Pass `--force` only when replacing conflicting assets is intentional.

`bootstrap-existing --interactive` uses `questionary` to prompt for repository path, asset groups, selected profiles, and whether to apply changes. It still defaults to dry-run behavior unless write confirmation is selected.

Use `--asset-group` with `audit` or `bootstrap-existing` to scope work to selected groups: `agent`, `config`, `design`, `docs`, `memory`, `metadata`, `models`, `plan`, `privacy`, `prompts`, `repomap`, `safety`, `sandbox`, `secrets`, `skills`, `tools`, or `worktrees`.

Audit output includes the comparison basis, selected option set, and asset groups. This is important when checking whether a full-adoption audit is using default selections or explicit selections.

Use `resolve-conflicts` before touching user-owned conflicts. It is read-only and previews merge strategies such as heading-based `AGENTS.md` additions and line-union `.gitignore` additions.

## Prompt Migration And Evals

For prompt DAGs, do not rewrite prompts first. Start by inventorying prompts, classifying each prompt's DAG role, and adding fixtures at meaningful node boundaries. Then apply GPT-5.5 prompt guidance with minimal diffs and behavior comparisons.

Recommended adoption:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-prompts --path /path/to/repo --prompt-profile prompt-migration-gpt55 --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-prompts --path /path/to/repo --prompt-profile prompt-evals-dag --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill prompt-migration --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill prompt-eval-design --apply
```

Use `hamilton-dag` where Hamilton is already used:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-repomap --path /path/to/repo --repomap-profile hamilton-dag --apply
```

Keep non-DAG helpers out of Hamilton modules when graph fingerprints are used for regression checks.

## Prompt Safety And Privacy

For policy, education, children, public sector, or user-facing AI systems, add:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-safety --path /path/to/repo --safety-profile prompt-output-safety --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-privacy --path /path/to/repo --privacy-profile data-privacy-review --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-public-interest --path /path/to/repo --public-interest-profile child-rights-digital --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill prompt-output-safety --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill privacy-review --apply
```

## Bootstrap Metadata

Existing repository bootstrap should write `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` with `bootstrap_mode: existing_repository`. The current implementation records assets actually written by the operation and does not claim skipped conflicts as generated assets.

Generated asset records include `content_sha256` for written non-metadata assets. This allows `check` to report generated assets as `ok`, `modified`, `missing`, or `unchecked`.

Use `diff-upstream-candidate` after local changes to classify generated asset drift before proposing improvements back to the Reference Source. It is read-only and should be paired with the `upstream-improvement` skill before copying downstream content upstream. Current Reference Source comparison is advisory; template-variable-heavy assets may report `reference-may-have-changed` until Bootstrap Metadata records richer template context.

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill upstream-improvement --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo
```

Use `upgrade` to preview upgrade readiness without writing files:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo
```

The current `upgrade` command is read-only. It reports assets that need user review, assets that block a future write-capable upgrade, and assets that are unavailable for upgrade until richer template context is recorded.

Future refresh behavior should remain explicit rather than live sync. The intended next evolution is a preview-first `upgrade` or `refresh-selected-assets` workflow that compares selected generated assets, skill templates, profile output, and `.agents/skill-sources.yml` provenance against the current Reference Source. Apply mode should be opt-in, scoped by asset group, and conservative: update unchanged generated files, line-union `.gitignore`, preview heading-based `AGENTS.md` merges, and keep `README.md`/`plan.md` manual-review by default.

For Reference Source maintenance, use `check-skill-sources` before refreshing vendored skills. It compares recorded GitHub skill source URLs with local vendored skills and reports missing support files without writing changes.

Potential future fields:

```yaml
bootstrap_mode: existing_repository
adopted_assets: []
conflicts: []
```

These fields should not be added to schema v1 until implementation needs them.

## Current Status

The first implementation can audit and add the same selected asset set used by new repository generation. It reports assets as missing, present, or conflicting and writes only missing assets unless `--force` is used.

Targeted add commands reuse the same bootstrap engine with narrower asset groups, so adopting one class of defaults does not also create unrelated files.

## Advice

`advise` is read-only. It detects coarse repository signals such as docs, plans, tests, CI, frontend files, container config, agent files, and bootstrap metadata. Recommendation logic lives in `src/repo_familiar/advice_dag.py`, a Hamilton-compatible node module that keeps non-DAG command formatting helpers outside the graph. It recommends one of these stages:

- `research-heavy`
- `prototype-fast`
- `implementation-planning`
- `production-maintenance`

It also recommends asset groups, profile families, skills, and next commands. Use `--intent` when the planned work is known, such as `significant-refactor`, `prompt-migration`, `production-maintenance`, `security-review`, or `docs-setup`.

## Memory Usage

Use memory tools when they speed recall without replacing committed context:

- At session start, query for project decisions, conventions, recurring errors, and current stage.
- After resolving a non-obvious bug, store the lesson and verification method.
- After accepting an ADR or resolving terminology, store the decision summary and link to the committed doc.
- After advancing stages, store why the stage changed and which profiles/tools were selected.
- Do not store secrets, private personal data, or machine-specific paths.

## Local Secrets

The safest local default is to keep secret values outside the repository and inject them at process start.

Recommended options:

- `kvenv-azure-keyvault`: `.env` contains `kv://` references; `kvenv` resolves them from Azure Key Vault when launching a command.
- `onepassword-op`: 1Password stores the values; `op run` or `op inject` provides them to the process.
- `dotenv-local`: `.env.example` is committed, `.env` is ignored, and local values remain machine-local.
- `sops-age`: selected secret/config files are committed encrypted with SOPS and age. Pass `--sops-age-recipient` to generate `.sops.yaml` and the `secrets/` workflow docs; without recipients, only advisory guidance is generated.

For all options, never store real secret values in `.agents/*.yml`, `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml`, memory, or committed docs.

## Accessibility Scanning

For repositories with frontend code, Quarto sites, design docs, or other user-facing web outputs, `advise` recommends:

- `a11y-scanner` tool profile
- `design-a11y` design profile
- `a11y-web-scan` skill

Adopt them with:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-tool --path /path/to/repo --tool a11y-scanner --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-design --path /path/to/repo --design-profile design-a11y --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill a11y-web-scan --apply
```

For reporting, borrow the ADT Studio pattern: show selected pages/routes, rule deltas, top violations, and a manual-review split of confirmed, resolved, and residual items. Automated scans should be paired with manual keyboard, focus, screen reader, contrast, and responsive checks.
